classification.difficultyReason: Apply the taught twelve-hour cycle, discard complete cycles and advance the displayed time by the remaining two hours.

questions.mappingNote: The closest supplied catalogue skill is adding positive integers: the directly assessed calculation adds two remaining hours to the given clock time. No modular-arithmetic skill is present in the supplied catalogue.
questions.methodNote: Page 1 explains the twelve-hour clock cycle and Example 1 divides an elapsed time into complete cycles plus remaining hours. Apply that same method to 50 hours.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Reduce a forward time shift to whole twelve-hour cycles and add the remaining hours.

classification.difficultyReason: Reduce 100 hours modulo 12, then count backwards and wrap past 12 to interpret the displayed hour.

questions.mappingNote: This question applies the taught twelve-hour cycle backwards. Integer subtraction is the closest supplied catalogue skill; modular arithmetic has no dedicated supplied ID.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Reduce the elapsed time by complete twelve-hour cycles, then subtract the remaining hours across twelve.

classification.difficultyReason: Use division by seven to find the weekday shift; the harder part requires interpreting the remainder as a backwards shift.

questions.mappingNote: Both parts apply the seven-day cycle from Example 2. Part a advances by the remainder; part b moves backwards by the remainder. Integer division is the closest supplied catalogue skill.
questions.methodNote: Page 1 Example 2 divides the elapsed days by seven and interprets the remainder as a weekday shift. The surrounding explanation allows counting forwards or backwards; page 2 defines congruence through equal remainders.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Find remainders on division by seven and interpret forward and backward weekday shifts.

classification.difficultyReason: Start at each supplied positive residue and repeatedly add its modulus, directly extending the taught same-remainder sequences.

questions.mappingNote: All four parts extend the same-remainder sequences by adding the modulus. Divisibility tests is the closest supplied catalogue skill because congruence requires differences divisible by the modulus.
questions.methodNote: Page 1 demonstrates repeated modular counting; page 2 defines congruent integers by their common remainder and gives the sequence 2, 7, 12, 17 modulo 5.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Generate positive integers with a specified remainder by repeatedly adding the modulus. The catalogue has no dedicated modular-arithmetic skill.

classification.difficultyReason: Apply division with a non-negative remainder; negative inputs require choosing the lower multiple so the residue lies between zero and the modulus.

questions.mappingNote: Every part asks for the remainder of one integer on division by its stated modulus. The closest available catalogue skill is divisibility-tests; no induction or polynomial remainder method is assessed.
questions.methodNote: Use integer division a=qn+r with 0≤r<n, then identify r as the least residue. Page 2 Example 3(c) demonstrates a negative quotient; Example 4 demonstrates least residues including zero.

classification.difficultyReason: Use the demonstrated difference test, handling negative signs and expressing each difference as a multiple of the stated modulus.

questions.mappingNote: All six parts directly assess the integer divisibility proof demonstrated in Example 5; prove-results-integers is the closest supplied catalogue skill.
questions.methodNote: Two integers are congruent modulo n exactly when their difference is a multiple of n. Page 3, Example 5 demonstrates this method, including subtraction of a negative integer.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Direct application of the taught difference criterion for congruence, including negative integers.

classification.difficultyReason: Reduce sums and products modulo 10 to determine their units digits.

questions.methodNote: Find units digits by calculating remainders modulo 10. Page 3 demonstrates replacing summands with their units digits; pages 4–5 establish addition and multiplication of congruences.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Reduce sums and products modulo 10 to determine their units digits.

previousLocalDifficulty.difficultyReason: Reduce both factors modulo 8 and multiply their remainders.
